Estimate a large number of Backlog Items, such as User Stories or features, quickly. This is useful when attempting to estimate a lot of work as is typical during Product Backlog creation or release planning. This approach provides a better overview of effort segmentation, making comparisons easier.

To execute Affinity Estimation:

  1. Obtain the following supplies:
    a. White board or large chart to display on a wall
    b. Tape
    c. Index cards
    d. List of defined User Stories

  2. Prepare for the estimation exercise:
    a. Determine appropriate participants to invite; typically the entire Development Team is involved unless the team is not fully formed in which case external experts would be allowed
    b. Send invites and confirm availability

  3. Draw a horizontal axis on the whiteboard/wall marking the far left side with “small” and the far right side with “large” 

  4. Write or print each User Story on an individual index card

  5. Shuffle the index cards so the order is random 

  6. Gather participants in the same room or area as the whiteboard

  7. Start with one participant at a time and have the individual use a few moments (typically no longer than 30 seconds) to:
    a. Select an index card
    b. Decide where on the axis the User Story should be placed relative to the small and large notations c. Explain their supporting rationale: All participants should agree what will happen in the event this process exceeds one minute; for example, the explanation is stopped and the User Story is immediately placed on the axis

  8. Proceed to the next participant and have them follow the same process

  9. Continue this procedure until there are several User Stories on the board; at this point, participants have the option to either:
    a. Select a new User Story and assign it to a column with a supporting explanation, or
    b. Select an already assigned User Story whose placement they disagree with and place it elsewhere on the axis
    (Note: a supporting rationale for the reassignment is required and the time limit still applies)

  10. Allow all participants the option to pass on any given turn

  11. Once all of the User Stories have been set on the axis and every participant signals a they are complete, the participants should inspect the result and identify clusters of User Stories with respect to size:
    a. User Stories clustered closest to the “small” end of the axis are assigned an estimate of 2 Story Points
    b. User Stories clustered second closest to the “small” end of the axis are assigned an estimate of 3 Story Points

This is continued until all User Stories, or features, are assigned an estimate.
